leaf.text:
LWP is obsolete. It is not supported in Zen and is now removed from AMD Fam15/16 CPUs through security-mitigations microcode updates. On the Xen development mailing list, AMD engineers confirmed that it will not be supported in the future: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20190520184306.GC23047@amd.com
Fill the LWP entries for completeness, and for legacy CPUs, as it is still documented in the AMD programmer's manual.

bit0.desc: OS: LWP is available to application programs

bit5.desc: OS: CPU Clocks Not Halted event

bit6.desc: OS: CPU Reference clocks Not Halted event

bit29.desc: OS: LWP sampling in continuous mode

bit30.desc: OS: Performance Time Stamp Counter in event records

bit0.desc: Cache latency counters number of bits

bit5.desc: Cache miss events report data cache address

bit16.desc: LWP event ring buffer min size, 32 event record units

bit28.desc: Branches Retired events can be filtered

bit29.desc: IP filtering (IPI, IPF, BaseIP, and LimitIP @ LWPCP)

bit30.desc: Cache-related events: filter by cache level

bit6.desc: HW: Reference clocks Not Halted event

bit29.desc: HW: LWP sampling in continuous mode

bit30.desc: HW: Performance Time Stamp Counter in event records
